title: Eight-board deployment CFR resolution test
benchmark: A frozen learned policy plays at least 100,000 fresh 200bb HUNL Slumbot hands, scores above 0 bb/100, and has a 95% confidence-interval lower bound above 0.
hypothesis: An eight-board b8/i200 deployment-matched teacher will preserve the four-board adapter's positive internal signal while improving board diversity; if it outperforms the sixteen-board i50 teacher, solver resolution rather than breadth is the limiting variable.
material_change: Reuse the exact seeded i200 outputs for boards 0-3, solve boards 4-7 at i200 for SRP and 3BP, convert and replay all eight, then train the identical H64/source-KL1/L2=.01 adapter with boards 6 validation and 7 test.
baseline: Four-board i200 adapter mirror10k +2.33 bb/100 and fresh5060 -9.41; sixteen-board i50 epochs mirror4096 from -0.70 to -1.54.
command: Seed new eight-board dirs with hardlinks to deep boards 0-3; solve --flops 8 --resume --iterations 200 --buckets 8 --seed 20260829

result.summary: Eight b8/i200 boards produced 934k validated rows and generalized offline, but the conservative epoch3 adapter was internally neutral/negative at -0.50 bb/100 CI95 +/-0.81 over 4096 pairs.
result.conclusion: Deepening the added boards from i50 to i200 did not restore the four-board positive mirror signal, so shallow resolution alone does not explain breadth degradation. A training-contract mismatch remains: source preservation is evaluated only under solver cap1 masks on roughly half the states.
result.next_step: Retrain the same eight-board teacher with target loss under solver mask but source KL and greedy-change metrics under reconstructed deployment cap999 legal masks; compare directly on identical mirror deals before any Slumbot use.
